author: blu
body: The VM is launched DIRECTLY rather than through Start-VmRun. These samples crash in well under a second, and Start-VmRun sleeps 500 ms, treats an already-exited process as a failed launch and retries four times before answering null, so every sample reported FAIL (vm start) and the file asserted nothing. That logic was not wrong when it was written: it was written against QEMU, whose chardev is server=on,wait=on, so QEMU blocks before running the guest until the harness connects and the process was still alive at the 500 ms check. codex-vm has no such wait, and the choice between them is not a flag but a Test-Path on the codex-vm binary, so the day codex-vm.exe landed in the depot this test broke in every workspace at once with no changelist touching it.

author: blu
body: exc-stack-heap carries a ninety-second budget where the fault samples take under a second, and the reason is historical. Measured 2026-07-26 on the depot seed it never terminated at all: a run left going for over twelve hours never printed OUT OF MEMORY and never exited, and codex-vm's own timeout did not stop it, so the script carried it as KNOWN FAILING and the budget was sized to fail fast rather than to let it finish.

author: blu
body: NeedFrames asserts the guest's RBP frame walk actually produced frames. exc-deep-frames faults six non-tail recursions down, so a working walk reports at least three and a walk that silently stopped reports none; without it the sample would pass on the !EXC= line alone and the capability could rot unnoticed. The shallower samples fault at the top of the stack, which the handler's own RSP switch overwrites before the walk runs, so they are not expected to yield a chain.
